item.base_system: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) elemental powders
item.intervention: Addition of stearic acid (3.5 wt. %) as process control agent and carbon/oxygen source
item.processing: High energy planetary ball milling for 39 h at 300 rpm in pure argon atmosphere
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compression tests at strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
item.structure_change: Formation of in-situ TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles via reaction during milling and sintering
item.property_change: Compressive fracture strength increased to 1542 MPa (compared to 1010 MPa of as-cast alloy)
item.attributed_mechanism: Stearic acid acted as source of elements carbon and oxygen for in-situ formation of reinforced particles
quotes: The stearic acid was introduced as process control agent (PCA) to prevent cold welding as well as particle agglomeration, and also acted as additive for generating particulate reinforced HEA composite.
During the process of high energy ball-milling, PCA is used to not only prevent cold-welding, but also act as the source of the elements carbon and oxygen.
The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina.

item.intervention: Consolidation via Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 1700 °C for 30 min under 30 MPa axial pressure
item.processing: SPS (D25/3, FCT) with heating rate of 100 K/min, held at 1700 °C for 30 min, furnace cooled
item.structure_change: Highly densified composite with BCC matrix, 32.2 vol.% TiC, and 7.0 vol.% Al2O3; average particle sizes of 4.60 μm (TiC) and 1.57 μm (Al2O3)
item.property_change: Compressive fracture strength of 1542 MPa, an increase of approximately 50% compared to as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA
item.attributed_mechanism: Second phase strengthening, grain refinement, and solid solution effect from interstitial C and O
quotes: Subsequently, the as-milled powders were consolidated by SPS (D25/3, FCT, Munich, Germany) under 30 MPa axial pressure at 1700 °C with the heating rate of 100 K/min.

With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA.
The composite created a kind of material with highly improved compressive strength, increasing from 1010 MPa to 1542 MPa.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: As-milled NbMoCrTiAl powder mixture. Intervention: Consolidation via Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at 1700 °C for 30 min under 30 MPa axial pressure. Property change: Compressive fracture strength of 1542 MPa, an increase of approximately 50% compared to as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA. Mechanism: Second phase strengthening, grain refinement, and solid solution effect from interstitial C and O. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Subsequently, the as-milled powders were consolidated by SPS (D25/3, FCT, Munich, Germany) under 30 MPa axial pressure at 1700 °C with the heating rate of 100 K/min."

item.intervention: Introduction of interstitial Carbon (1.28 at. %) and Oxygen (0.69 at. %)
item.processing: In-situ formation during ball milling and SPS
item.structure_change: Interstitial atoms dissolved in BCC phase creating strain fields
item.property_change: Significant increase in strength attributed to solution strengthening
item.attributed_mechanism: Interstitial atoms produce substantial strain fields interacting with gliding dislocations
quotes: In this study, the BCC phase contains 0.69 at. % O and 1.28 at. % C, which may cause significant increase in strength because these two interstitial atoms have a substantially smaller size than any of the metal atoms in the HEA.
These interstitial atoms will produce a substantial strain field, with which gliding dislocations will interact.
Therefore, we may reasonably conclude that solution-strengthening effect resulted in the improved mechanical properties.

It can be found that introduction of brittle ceramic reinforcements would significantly increase mechanical properties of the material.
The remarkable increase in mechanical properties can be attributed to second phase strengthening effect, grain refinement and solid solution effect.

item.intervention: Grain refinement via Powder Metallurgy (P/M) processing
item.processing: Ball milling followed by SPS at 1700 °C
item.structure_change: Grain size reduced from ~100 μm (as-homogenized) to much lower values in composite
item.property_change: Contribution to increased compressive strength (1542 MPa)
item.attributed_mechanism: Grain refinement strengthening and hard phases acting as barriers to grain growth
quotes: The grain size of the as-homogenized NbMoCrTiAl phase is about 100 μm, while that of the composite is much lower.
This is because the PM process is an effective approach to refine grains compared to arc-melting.
In addition, the hard phases evenly distributed at the grain boundary, acting as the barrier of grain growth.

item.intervention: Formation of TiC phase with Nb solute
item.structure_change: TiC phase lattice constant increased to 0.435 nm (vs 0.433 nm pure TiC) due to Nb solution
item.property_change: Contribution to overall mechanical property improvement
item.attributed_mechanism: Solution of atoms with large radius (Nb) in TiC lattice causing lattice parameter change and strengthening
quotes: With regard to the carbide, the lattice constant of TiC (0.435 nm) is slightly larger than pure TiC (0.433 nm).
The different crystal parameter may result from the solution of atoms with large radius, such as element Nb (r = 0.148 nm) in this composite.

This certain concentration of Nb incorporated during grain growth agrees with the large solubility of solute Nb-carbide in solvent TiC mainly because of their largest negative value of Hmix and identical crystal structure.
